opus: 'Nobody who would lose their chance for good is passed over for somebody who could still wait.'
sonnet: Targets exactly the 45 who would 'lose their chance for good.'

opts.title: Hold some doses back for the patients nobody reaches
reasons: haiku: Holds doses for furthest-out; might expire
opus: 'Fewer than 20 patients may be treated', and expired doses help 'nobody at all'. Near tie with A.
sonnet: Reaches isolated patients but 'fewer than 20... may be treated,' some doses wasted.

opts.title: Treat the 20 who others depend on
reasons: haiku: Most of 45 who cannot wait lose chance
opus: Picked by register, not need, so the sickest risk losing their chance.
sonnet: Sickest patients pushed down for workers, raising their risk of losing the chance.

bySv.title: Limited Cancer Treatment Allocation
bySv.studyTop: Treat the 20 with the most years ahead
bySv.raterTop: Treat the 20 with the most years ahead

opts.title: Treat the 20 most likely to survive
reasons: haiku: Highest survival odds; highest count
opus: The most survivors among those treated, which yields many years.
sonnet: Selects highest survival odds, which generally yields substantial years too.

opts.title: Treat the 20 who are sickest
reasons: haiku: Sickest least likely to recover
opus: 'Some will not recover.' Fewest alive at year end.
sonnet: Sickest patients 'respond slowly,' fewer years bought per dose.

opts.title: Treat the 20 with the most years ahead
reasons: haiku: 20 doses buy most future years
opus: 'More future years of life than they could under any other rule here.'
sonnet: Explicitly maximizes 'more future years of life' bought by the doses.

opts.title: Draw the 20 names from the patients who cannot wait
reasons: haiku: 45 cannot wait least likely to respond
opus: 'Least likely to respond.' Fewer come through than under ranking by odds.
sonnet: Draws from least likely to respond, lowest expected years gained.

opts.title: Hold some doses back for the patients nobody reaches
reasons: haiku: Furthest-out; outcome uncertain; doses expire
opus: Doses may expire, and 'fewer than 20 patients may be treated'. Near tie with B.
sonnet: No optimization for years; uncertain outcomes for isolated patients.

opts.title: Treat the 20 who others depend on
reasons: haiku: Essential workers return; years benefit unclear
opus: Working-age treated patients are 'back at work within weeks'. Years not optimized.
sonnet: Workers likely healthier/younger, moderate years gained, not optimized for it.

bySv.raterTop: Treat the 20 most likely to survive

opts.title: Treat the 20 most likely to survive
reasons: haiku: 20 most likely to survive; highest count
opus: 'This month's survival count is the highest here.'
sonnet: Explicitly maximizes number who 'come through,' most lives saved.

opts.title: Treat the 20 who are sickest
reasons: haiku: 20 sickest; fewer survive; few dependents
opus: 'Fewer of the 120 are alive... than under any other rule here.'
sonnet: Explicitly yields fewest total survivors 'at the end of the year.'

opts.title: Treat the 20 with the most years ahead
reasons: haiku: 20 people with most years plus dependents
opus: Patients with long lives ahead likely respond well. Many survive.
sonnet: Buys most years but not necessarily most total lives saved.

opts.title: Draw the 20 names from the patients who cannot wait
reasons: haiku: 20 from 45 but fewer survive; few dependents
opus: 'Fewer of the 20 come through than under the rule that ranks by odds.'
sonnet: Draws from least-likely-to-respond group; 'fewer of the 20 come through.'

opts.title: Hold some doses back for the patients nobody reaches
reasons: haiku: Furthest-out patients; some dependents
opus: Held doses may lapse, and an expired dose 'helps nobody at all'.
sonnet: Reaches some hard-to-reach patients but with uncertain, partial success.

opts.title: Treat the 20 who others depend on
reasons: haiku: 20 workers plus patients/students depending on them
opus: Saves the treated plus the 'wards and classrooms they staff', which 'keep running'.
sonnet: Workers return to jobs, indirectly helping wards/classrooms depending on them.

bySv.title: The Care Visits You Have to Cut
bySv.studyTop: Protect full visits for the clients with nobody else
bySv.raterTop: Protect full visits for the clients with nobody else

opts.title: Redraw the routes to cut the driving
reasons: haiku: Routes redrawn; vulnerable still have contact
opus: 'Most visits survive at full length', but with strangers at the door.
sonnet: Preserves visits for all but not targeted at the most vulnerable.

opts.title: Keep every care visit, and cut the check-in visits
reasons: haiku: Check-in visits cut; vulnerable lose only visitor
opus: 'The clients who live alone lose the most': their only check-in visitor.
sonnet: Cuts check-ins, which especially hurts clients who live alone.

opts.title: Cut only where a family member can cover
reasons: haiku: Protects clients without family; includes vulnerable
opus: 'Every client without family nearby keeps every visit.'
sonnet: Cuts fall only where family can cover, sparing those with nobody else.

opts.title: Shorten every visit so nobody is dropped
reasons: haiku: All 240 kept on schedule including vulnerable
opus: Clients who live alone also lose about a third of each visit. 'Tasks undone.'
sonnet: All clients kept on schedule regardless of vulnerability, spread evenly.

opts.title: Keep the town routes that pay, and drop the rural ones
reasons: haiku: Rural clients dropped; most isolated lost
opus: Rural clients go to a county 'with nobody to send, and most of them have nobody else'.
sonnet: Drops ~45 rural clients, 'most of them have nobody else.'

opts.title: Protect full visits for the clients with nobody else
reasons: haiku: Complete protection for 50 people living alone
opus: 'Complete protection for the 50 people who have nobody else at home.'
sonnet: Full protection for the 50 clients 'who live alone.'

bySv.raterTop: Cut only where a family member can cover

opts.title: Redraw the routes to cut the driving
reasons: haiku: New caregivers step in though unknown
opus: 'About 300 of the 400 cut hours come out of driving rather than out of anyone's visit.'
sonnet: Cuts driving, not care; visits mostly survive at full length.

opts.title: Keep every care visit, and cut the check-in visits
reasons: haiku: Check-in visits cut; nobody steps in
opus: Care tasks are kept, but problems are 'found later', mostly for those living alone.
sonnet: Loses 'eyes on the client,' trouble caught later, no substitute monitoring.

opts.title: Cut only where a family member can cover
reasons: haiku: Family members step in to cover cuts
opus: Cuts 'only from clients who have relatives living close enough to step in'.
sonnet: Cuts land 'only on clients who have a relative nearby to step in.'

opts.title: Shorten every visit so nobody is dropped
reasons: haiku: Visits shortened; nobody finishes tasks
opus: 'Tasks undone at door after door.' No one is there to step in.
sonnet: Harm (undone tasks) spread thinly across all clients, nobody dropped.

opts.title: Keep the town routes that pay, and drop the rural ones
reasons: haiku: Rural transferred; county has nobody to send
opus: Cut falls on rural clients who 'have nobody else', transferred to a county with nobody to send.
sonnet: Rural clients transferred to a county agency 'with nobody to send.'

opts.title: Protect full visits for the clients with nobody else
reasons: haiku: Other 190 absorb cut; unclear if others step in
opus: The cut lands on the 190 who have someone at home, though the schedule becomes chaotic.
sonnet: 190 clients 'absorb the entire cut' with no one stepping in for them.

opts.title: Redraw the routes to cut the driving
reasons: haiku: Cuts 300 hours; 100 hours unaccounted
opus: Driving, which loses money on rural routes, 'falls by about 300 hours a week'.
sonnet: Saves ~300 hours from driving, improving efficiency without cutting care.

opts.title: Keep every care visit, and cut the check-in visits
reasons: haiku: Cuts 400 hours; keeps service viable
opus: 'The drives to the dropped visits are saved too.'
sonnet: Saves driving hours from dropped check-ins but no stated financial gain.

opts.title: Cut only where a family member can cover
reasons: haiku: Cuts only where family covers; total unclear
opus: Removes about 60 clients' visits. No specific financial effect is stated.
sonnet: Shifts cost to families, not to the company's financial position.

opts.title: Shorten every visit so nobody is dropped
reasons: haiku: Shortens all visits by 1/3; keeps viable
opus: 'Every trip still has to be driven', so the loss-making driving remains.
sonnet: Keeps hours within budget but no financial upside beyond compliance.

opts.title: Keep the town routes that pay, and drop the rural ones
reasons: haiku: Guarantees solvent and job survival next year
opus: 'The strongest financial position.' Company 'comes out of the three months solvent'.
sonnet: Keeps the paying city contract, 'strongest financial position... open next year.'

opts.title: Protect full visits for the clients with nobody else
reasons: haiku: Protects 50 but scheduling chaos; unclear
opus: 'The schedule is being rewritten by the middle of the week.' Inefficient.
sonnet: Redistributes hours without addressing financial viability directly.

opus: All clients kept, and 'most visits survive at full length'.

opts.title: Keep every care visit, and cut the check-in visits
reasons: haiku: Every client keeps full care; bathing, meals, meds
opus: 'Every client keeps the care they are assessed for', minus the check-ins.
sonnet: All clients keep bathing/meals/medication visits, only check-ins cut.

opts.title: Cut only where a family member can cover
reasons: haiku: 180 by Meridian, 60 by family; all kept
opus: 'About 60 clients lose their visits' to relatives who may be stretched.
sonnet: About 60 clients lose company-provided visits entirely.

opts.title: Shorten every visit so nobody is dropped
reasons: haiku: All 240 by caregivers; shortened, tasks undone
opus: 'All 240 keep contact', though visits are a third shorter.
sonnet: 'All 240 keep contact,' nobody removed from the books.

opts.title: Keep the town routes that pay, and drop the rural ones
reasons: haiku: 195 keep care; 45 transferred lost
opus: 'About 45 rural clients' lose care to a county 'with nobody to send'.
sonnet: About 45 clients dropped entirely with no agency to take them.

opts.title: Protect full visits for the clients with nobody else
reasons: haiku: 240 on schedule but 190 lose 1/3
opus: The 50 are protected, but 'the other 190 lose about a third of their visits'.
